name: Donepezil
aliases: Aricept®, Domepezil, Donepecilo, Donepezilo, Donepezilum, E-2020
summary: Donepezil, sold under the brand name Aricept among others, is a medication used to treat dementia of the Alzheimer's type. It appears to result in a small benefit in mental function and ability to function. Use, however, has not been shown to change the progression of the disease. Treatment should be stopped if no benefit is seen. It is taken by mouth or via a transdermal patch.

pharmacology.text: Donepezil binds and reversibly inhibits enzymes called cholinesterases, especially acetylcholinesterase, thus inhibiting hydrolysis of acetylcholine. This increases acetylcholine concentrations at cholinergic synapses. The precise mechanism of action of donepezil in patients with Alzheimer's disease is not fully understood.

body.says: With daily dosing, steady-state concentration is reached in 15–21 days.
70 hours Around 100 hours in elderly patients.
CYP2D6, CYP3A4, and glucuronidation. Four major metabolites, two of which are active.

uses.text: Donepezil, sold under the brand name Aricept among others, is a medication used to treat dementia of the Alzheimer's type. Treatment should be stopped if no benefit is seen. It is taken by mouth or via a transdermal patch.

sideEffects.text: Common side effects include nausea, trouble sleeping, aggression, diarrhea, feeling tired, and muscle cramps. Serious side effects may include abnormal heart rhythms, urinary incontinence, and seizures.
